body: The driver verb table and schema: a fifteenth verb `layout` at the instance level, its one required argument of the existing element id kind, lookup by name, its level check, and the schema's verb count moving from 14 to 15.

Validation of the layout call before anything runs: a missing or malformed id refused with the existing malformed cause; an id the screen does not read refused stale or not-found as the session's layout read refuses today; no new refusal cause, cause order, session error, exit status or node key.

The session's layout read as the executor arm of run: a reading verb, no step, pump, tick, settle or load wait, the held instance and its state unchanged, a refusal changing nothing and echoing no input.

The layout answer's JSON written form: one line, stable id strings, closed words and numbers only — never a node id, page text, authored style value, colour or control value, nothing of the screen beyond that.

The element the engine cannot explain answers a closed word of its own instead of placed by the engine as a block with no container and both causes layout; every layout reader word, the new one among them, read on a fixture, in both layout modes.
The session socket: the call carries the new verb inside the unchanged v3 wire, its answer within the answer bounds, refused and oversize answers as for every reading verb.

The escher-session command line: `layout --id {id} --session {dir}` as a command form, its stdout answer line, its refusal line with remedy and its exit statuses as the other instance verbs have them, the usage line and help naming it, no caller input echoed.

The MCP role: a tool `layout` listed in tools/list after actions and before help, its id argument, its result text decoded whole, a refused call returned as a refused tool result, help parity with the command line, and the tool count moving to fifteen.

Recording and replay: a layout step recorded into a check with its answer kept whole, the check read back taking tool layout among the instance verbs, replay replaying it through the ordinary call path, the same check on the socket and MCP surfaces.
help describes layout from the verb tables with its result fields, on the command line and over MCP alike.
The actions answer: every node it lists takes the verb word layout with no cause, the answer still holding no value.

Re-read the twelve cross-OS answer digests (snapshot, lint and actions on six served tasks, at boot and after one step) on linux x86_64, windows x86_64 and macOS aarch64: the actions digests move with the new verb word, the snapshot and lint digests hold; the comparison holds no shot.

Log lines: the command span records verb and, refused, cause alone — no id, no reading, no count of the answer; the MCP tool_call span holds tool and ending as for every tool; stand and host logs carry no ids, names or screen content.

The capability statement, read from and pinned to the driver schema: its verb list and counts held to the schema by the CI script check, the README tool count with it, and the v030-11 claim naming the checks that prove it.
The gate block lists the doc leg, since the chunk edits public doc comments, beside fast and the legs the touchpoints call for.
Driver verbs over a held instance are tested by integration checks of the executor on the stand; command-line checks run the package's own binary; MCP is tested both as a child and in process.
A fork that is the founder's while he is away is taken at its most conservative option and written down, not asked; the verb's form is ruled and not reopened.

body_fields.convention: each new socket, command-line or MCP session check is unix-gated, owns and reaps its host, sends child streams to null and drains host pipes, and sits in one integration test target per file sharing the one session-check module
each new stand check runs on the bundled pinned font without skipping, in both layout modes, with no sleep or wall-clock read, and holds the zero-failure repeat budget
each new test pins its expected value as a literal, prints no argument value on failure, is controlled red-before-green, and a table-driven test asserts its row count
each new committed recorded check is byte-equal to the binary's recording, holds no screenshot step and no private data, and is kept fresh
each new fixture or test datum is stated in code, shared fixtures in one module, the stand booting offline
each new log line of the session or stand holds fixed words and counts only, no ids, names or screen content, and test output never reaches agent-run events
each change to a CI leg or gate runs through the leg script, locked, with the fast leg gating the rest and per-package green not read as workspace green

The cold-agent pipe: its bar, events, verdict, isolation and live run are out of scope; the cold-agent bar counting the read is another carry.
The agent-run five-command contract: its verbs, selections, events, state and exit codes do not change.
Pixel and paint rows: screenshots, PNG decoding, frames compared whole, scrollbar thumbs, select list painting, box-shadow and font embolden witnesses; the layout answer carries no pixels.
Contrast and lint rows: the contrast formula and required ratio, and the lint defect kinds and order, are read by other verbs this chunk leaves as they are.
Virtual time and timers: advance, the clock, timer ticks and settle passes; the layout read advances, ticks and settles nothing.
Handler coverage: its line, limits, unreached screens and canvas handlers are not changed by a reading verb.
Mocking and network stand-ins: no stand-in, load page or provider is added or changed.
Upstream blitz rows: the blitz-tests manifest, upstream buffered-render and mounted-flush tests, blitz-dom fixtures and request stamping are not reached.
Typed password and type-on-select rows, and the acting verbs' changed-node results, belong to acting verbs; layout acts on nothing.
The CI package-install script and its exit codes, and the CI artifact names, are not changed by this chunk.
